rationale: A is more robust because it checks both necessary Eulerian conditions—every vertex has even degree and the graph is connected—before backtracking. B is somewhat more concise and well documented, but its parity-only precheck can send disconnected, even-degree inputs into an unnecessarily expensive exhaustive search. Although A could be improved further by constructing the circuit directly with Hierholzer's algorithm, its separation of feasibility checking from construction is clear and handles impossible cases more predictably.
